subject: Post-demo follow-up: confirmation on prompt/output storage and residency
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <lucas.chen@curadata.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: confirmation on prompt/output storage and residency

Hi Lucas — great talking earlier, appreciate the demo time.  Quick recap and a small list of items we promised to confirm about prompt/response handling so your legal/compliance folks can review:  

- What Redwood stores by default (hosted): prompt text and model outputs are captured for debugging, performance analysis, and quality monitoring. We can provide more granular options for masking or not persisting certain fields.
- Retention windows (hosted defaults): 14 days for full payloads; aggregated usage metrics are retained longer for billing/analytics.
- Residency: hosted data is stored in the region you select; for EU residency we use eu-west-1, for US use us-west-2/us-east-1.
- Dedicated & Private: outputs can be configured to not be persisted (ephemeral-only) or retained according to your policy when Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment is used.
- Controls: field-level redaction, customer-provided KMS, audit logs, and on-demand deletion APIs are available on enterprise plans.

Action items I mentioned on the call:
1) Please confirm the environment you expect to use (hosted / dedicated / private) and which fields in prompts/outputs you consider PII.
2) For hosted consideration: confirm maximum acceptable retention (you mentioned <= 7 days).
3) If you need EU residency and specific deletion attestations, say so and I’ll loop in our security lead.

I attached a short post-demo note with the call highlights (post-demo-notes.txt). I’ve cc’d Kimberly so she can capture qualification details. Happy to jump on a quick call with legal if that helps.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: confirmation on prompt/output storage and residency

Jordan — thanks for the recap and the notes. A few clarifying items from our side so your security/legal can respond:  

- Environment: we prefer hosted for initial pilot but will likely move to Dedicated for production.
- PII scope: names, email addresses, SSNs (if they appear), and any patient identifiers in free text must not be retained in plain form.
- Retention requirement for hosted pilot: we require a maximum retention of 7 days for any prompt/response that contains PII. If that cannot be guaranteed on hosted, we need to know the mitigation (masking or not storing those fields).
- Residency: pilot traffic should be kept in us-west-2, production must be able to reside in eu-west-1 (we have EU patients later on).
- Deletion/attestation: legal wants the ability to request on-demand deletion and an attestation log within 48 hours.

Can your team confirm the technical guarantees above or provide options? If Hosted cannot meet the 7-day cap for PII-containing payloads, we need a concrete alternaive (e.g., immediate redaction or pilot in Dedicated).

Lucas Chen
Head of Product, CuraData
lucas.chen@curadata.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: confirmation on prompt/output storage and residency

Hi Lucas — Sean here, Head of Security. Thanks for the clear list — below are concrete options and the default behavior for each Redwood deployment mode. If you want an updated contract clause or an attestation, we can provide that as part of the enterprise onboarding.

Summary (short):
- Hosted API (standard): full request/response payloads are retained for 14 days by default to support debugging and abuse monitoring. For pilot customers that require tighter limits, we offer an enterprise-hosted profile that reduces retention to 0–7 days for payloads that are tagged as containing PII, or an option to redact PII at ingestion.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): data remains in tenant-isolated instances; you can configure no-persistence (ephemeral-only) for prompt outputs, or set a customer-defined TTL.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood control plane can be used while all logs and outputs are stored in your environment; retention and deletion are fully under your control.

Controls & guarantees we can provide: 
- Field-level redaction and dynamic masking at ingestion (we can drop or hash SSNs and other identified PII fields before writing to any logs).
- Customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, with HSM-backed keys available for enterprise customers.
- Audit logs and deletion APIs: we support exportable deletion attestations and an audit trail for deletion requests. Typical turnaround for attestation generation is 48 hours; we can add a SLA in the enterprise contract.
- Residency: Hosts in us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1 are available. For hosted pilot we can pin to us-west-2; production EU residency will require an enterprise residency selection.

Recommended next steps:
1) For your pilot: we recommend hosted with the enterprise-hosted privacy profile (reduces retention to 7 days or less for PII-tagged payloads) or pilot in Dedicated with ephemeral-only outputs if you prefer no hosted storage.
2) If you want attestations and contractual SLAs for deletion, I’ll route a paperwork template to Lauren and your legal team.
3) If you can share a short sample of the prompt schema (example fields flagged PII) we’ll prepare a masking/redaction plan and a quick config we can apply to the pilot.

I attached a short summary (redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf) which lists the controls and the default/enterprise options. I’ll also include our compliance pack if needed.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call with legal or security to finalize.

Sean Gallagher
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (3 pages)
